content:
Carla Ramos: quick question — for internal service-to-service contracts, are we happy with proto-first gRPC + a generated REST shim, or should we standardize on JSON/REST everywhere? :thinking:
Ben Li: my vote is proto-first. auto-generated shims (grpc-gateway) handle most cases and we get strong typing, backwards-compat rules, and better perf via HTTP/2.
Arjun Patel: +1 for proto-first, but mobile/web SDK teams will scream if we make them consume raw grpc. That's where a maintained REST shim / gateway matters.
Maya Chen: concern: codegen complexity and multi-language client support. We still have external partners that just curl JSON. We need a clear compatibility story.
Carla Ramos: proposal: make the canonical contract a .proto, publish codegen artifacts, and run a small "compat layer" service that exposes a stable REST surface. Internals call gRPC directly. Thoughts on centralizing the shim vs letting each service ship its own gateway?
Ben Li: central shim gives us consistent telemetry and quota enforcement at one place. Easier to roll out fallback behavior and circuit-breakers. But it's a single layer of failure and could add latency.
Arjun Patel: decentralized gateway (per-service) avoids an extra hop, but ops overhead multiplies. Also harder to enforce global policies (rate-limits, auth headers).
Maya Chen: telemetry/observability wins matter a lot — if we centralize, we can inject common tags: `x-rw-request-id`, `client_tier`, `model_version`, and ensure sampling/tracing headers propagate.
Diego (deploy-bot): deploy request queued for staging: `compat-gateway-v2` (image: infra/compat-gw:2026.04.2).
Carla Ramos: example of the proto with HTTP annotation I had in mind:
```
syntax = "proto3";
import "google/api/annotations.proto";
service Router {
  rpc Predict(PredictRequest) returns (PredictResponse) {
    option (google.api.http) = {
      post: "/v1/predict"
      body: "*"
    };
  }
}
message PredictRequest { string input = 1; string model = 2; }
```
Ben Li: that exact pattern works. We should enforce HTTP annotations in linter CI so the shim can be auto-generated.
Arjun Patel: what about streaming use-cases? grpc supports bidi streaming; shims often convert streaming to websockets or chunked responses which is awkward. We have a few realtime routes for KV-cache warmup that are streaming-heavy.
Maya Chen: we can mark streaming RPCs as gRPC-only and provide non-streaming fallbacks for partners. Document it in the API playbook.
Carla Ramos: quotas — where enforce? gateway (centralized) or service-level? If gateway enforces, it becomes a bottleneck for bursty traffic but simplifies accounting.
Ben Li: I'd push quota checks to the gateway for per-API keys and to services for per-user quotas tied to business logic. Two-layer check: cheap gate at gateway, authoritative check in service.
Arjun Patel: agree. Also, cache decisions (prefix caching, KV cache) should live in services; the gateway shouldn't attempt token-level cost accounting.
Maya Chen: rollout UX — prefer canarying by model-version at the gateway so we can route 5% to new model variant before services pick it up. Gateway must be able to route by header `x-model-variant`.
Carla Ramos: telemetry fields we want in every span: `request_id`, `caller_service`, `route`, `latency_ms`, `response_tokens` (if applicable), `model_version`. Also log sampling at 1% production, 100% on errors.
Arjun Patel: for schema evolution, let's adopt stable numeric field additions and deprecate names via annotations. Enforce removal only after 2 releases.
Diego (deploy-bot): canary rollout started for `compat-gateway-v2` -> 2% traffic.
Ben Li: implementation tasks I see: 1) proto linter rule + generator job, 2) central compat-gateway prototype with policy plugin for quotas/auth, 3) docs + SDK distribution plan for mobile/web.
Maya Chen: ops checklist: add tracing to gateway, ensure trace context propagation to services, add per-route dashboards in Console (p95, errors, request-rate, avg-resp-bytes).
Carla Ramos: final note — let's avoid making REST the source-of-truth. Proto-first seems to minimize drift. We'll draft an RFC outlining central vs local shim tradeoffs and propose the 2-layer quota approach. :thumbsup:
Ben Li: cool, I'll start an RFC draft and link proto linter examples.
Arjun Patel: I'll sketch edge cases for streaming and rollback scenarios.
Maya Chen: I'll add telemetry and dashboard requirements to the RFC.
Diego (deploy-bot): staging health check: compat-gateway-v2 -> OK (latency 48ms p95).
Carla Ramos: thanks all — leaving this thread for the RFC comments.
